_about.what: Published MNIST results for the LUT-DNN and weightless families, for the MNIST Phase 3 controlled comparison (docs/mnist/phase3-ledger.md). Citation only - nothing here was resynthesized by us.
_about.schema_from: cc/literature/jsc_literature.json - same field meanings, so cc/literature/table.py and plot.py can read both.
_about.warning_1_precision: MANY SOURCES ROUND ACCURACY TO WHOLE PERCENT. NeuraLUT Table III prints '96%' and '95%'. Our measured noise floor is 0.24 pp (docs/mnist/reduction-ledger.md), so a row printed as '96%' spans +/-0.5 pp -- TWICE our floor. Such a row cannot be ranked against ours, or against another rounded row. Use accuracy_precision to decide what a row can support. CONFIRMED 2026-08-13: SparseLUT Table IV prints the SAME models to two decimals -- NeuraLUT HDR-5L at 95.20%, PolyLUT HDR(D=2) at 95.42% -- against the '96%' their own papers print. Whether that is rounding-up or re-run variance is unresolved, but it means the '96%' rows should be treated as an upper bound, and our margin over them is if anything understated.
_about.warning_2_silicon: MNIST LUT-DNN work targets xcvu9p-flgb2104-2-i, a Virtex UltraScale+ with ~1.18M LUTs. Our XC7A35T has 20,800. NeuraLUT's MNIST model alone is 2.6x our whole device. Area is comparable as a NUMBER; 'fits on the board' is not, and speed grades differ.
_about.warning_3_polylut: RESOLVED 2026-08-13. PolyLUT HDR on MNIST is 96% / 70,673 LUTs, confirmed identically by THREE independent papers (its own arXiv:2309.02334 Table IV, NeuraLUT arXiv:2403.00849 Table III, PolyLUT-Add arXiv:2406.04910 Table III). The 97.5% / 75,131 figure appears in none of them; its probable source is the 2025 extended PolyLUT paper (arXiv:2501.08043, 'Ultra-low Latency Polynomial Inference with Hardware-Aware Structured Pruning'), which is a DIFFERENT and later configuration. Do not attribute it to the 2023 PolyLUT without reading that paper.

fields.dataset: mnist = the canonical 10,000-row test split. Unlike JSC there is only one MNIST, so no dataset-ambiguity correction applies (docs/mnist/phase3-ledger.md 2.3).
fields.accuracy_pct: As printed by the source. See accuracy_precision before comparing.
fields.accuracy_precision: whole_pct = printed as an integer percent, so the true value is +/-0.5 pp. one_dp / two_dp = printed to that many decimals.
fields.encoder_included: true = LUT count includes the input encoding stage. false = core only. n/a = the design consumes quantized inputs directly and has no separate encoder. unknown = not stated.
fields.confidence: verified = read from the cited paper's own table by us, directly, not via a summarizer. reported = from a secondary source quoting it. unverified = not yet seen.

_about.warning_4_weightless: The weightless family reports DIFFERENT METRICS. BTHOWeN gives real FPGA LUT counts on xc7z020clg400-1 -- same 7-series family and same -1 speed grade as our XC7A35T, so it is the closest silicon match in the whole table. ULEEN is ASIC (mm^2) plus model size (KiB) and has NO FPGA LUT number for MNIST. Accuracy is comparable for both; area is comparable only for BTHOWeN.
_about.warning_5_dwn_paper: The DWN paper's own MNIST rows are CORE-ONLY (encoder excluded). Ours are reported both ways in docs/results-mnist/sweep-results.json (dwn_core_luts vs dwn_top_luts). Comparing our dwn_top against their LUT column overstates our area by 1.4-2.5x and is the single easiest mistake to make in this table.

datasets.mnist: The canonical MNIST split: 60,000 train / 10,000 test, from mnist_784 in train-then-test order. Every published MNIST number uses this, so rows are directly comparable on accuracy.

results.notes: L-LUTs per layer 256,100,100,100,100,10; beta=2, F=6, L=4, N=16, S=2 (Table II). Vivado 2020.1, Flow_PerfOptimized_high, Out-of-Context, target clock 1-2 ns.

results.source: arXiv:2309.02334 Table IV (PolyLUT, own paper); corroborated by arXiv:2403.00849 Table III
results.notes: Architecture HDR = 256,100,100,100,100,10 nodes per layer, beta=2, F=6, polynomial degree 4 (Table III). RESOLVED: PolyLUT's own Table IV and NeuraLUT's Table III agree EXACTLY on all of accuracy/LUT/FF/Fmax/latency, and also agree on the FINN and hls4ml rows. The 97.5%/75,131 figure is therefore NOT PolyLUT's own claim -- it is a third-party re-run (likely SparseLUT, which optimises PolyLUT's connectivity). If it is ever used it needs its own row attributed to that paper, not to PolyLUT. THIRD independent confirmation of 96%/70,673: PolyLUT's own Table IV, NeuraLUT Table III, and PolyLUT-Add Table III all print it identically.
Binary, fully unfolded. FF not reported by the source. The only MNIST row here that uses BRAM. Cross-checked: identical in PolyLUT Table IV and NeuraLUT Table III.
12.5x NeuraLUT's area. Useful as the 'conventional NN toolchain' reference point. Cross-checked: identical in PolyLUT Table IV and NeuraLUT Table III.
Bits/Input (=z) 2, 1024 entries/filter, 2 hashes. Zybo Z7. 25 cycles/inference at 100 MHz.
Bits/Input 3, 2048 entries/filter. Zybo Z7. 37 cycles/inference.
Bits/Input 6, 8192 entries/filter, 4 hashes. Too large for the Zybo; paper moved it to a bigger part.
Iso-accuracy quantized DNN baseline. Uses 8 BRAM and 28 DSP -- NOT a LUT-only design, so not comparable to DWN on LUTs alone. 846 cycles/inference against BTHOWeN-Medium's 37.
Iso-accuracy CNN baseline from BTHOWeN Table IV. 33,615 cycles/inference.

⚠️ ASIC ONLY. Table III reports area in mm^2 (5.22) against Bit Fusion/LeNet-5, not FPGA LUTs. Table IV reports MODEL SIZE in KiB (262). ULN-S 96.20%, ULN-M 97.79%, ULN-L 98.46%. So ULEEN can be compared on ACCURACY and MODEL SIZE but NOT on FPGA area. Do not put it in a LUT-count column.
